previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting presented during a dialysis session with hypotension and bradycardia. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 8.6, leading to an idioventricular rhythm. He was treated in the emergency department with calcium gluconate, insulin, dextrose, and atropine, and underwent emergent hemodialysis, which normalized his potassium. His bradycardia and hypotension resolved, and he was weaned off dopamine. His home lisinopril dose was reduced to 20 mg daily to minimize potassium elevation risk. He reported mild diarrhea and possible missed medications prior to admission. Blood cultures showed no growth, and chest imaging revealed stable pleural effusions without signs of infection. He recovered well, restarted his insulin regimen, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete all dialysis sessions and monitor weight.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis,
now with fever, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and cough for four days. 
Evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal and lateral chest radiographs were obtained.

FINDINGS:  Bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left, are again
seen and grossly unchanged.  There is compressive atelectasis.  Linear
scarring in the left upper lobe is unchanged.  There is no pneumothorax. 
Median sternotomy wires are again seen.  Heart size is slightly enlarged, most
notably in the region of the right atrium.

IMPRESSION:  Persistent bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left. 
Right atrial enlargement.

INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis,
now with fever, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and cough for four days. 
Evaluate for appendicitis.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial CT images through the abdomen and pelvis were acquired after
administration of intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted
images were reviewed.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  Bilateral pleural effusions are again
seen, right greater than left, with compressive atelectasis.  Heart size is
top normal with right atrial enlargement.  The liver is hypoenhancing and
heterogeneous which may suggest fatty infiltration, although congestive heart
failure may partially contribute to this appearance.  The spleen is grossly
unremarkable.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy and surgical clips
are seen in the gallbladder fossa.  The pancreas is markedly atrophic. 
Calcification at the pancreatic head is again seen and may represent sequela
of prior pancreatitis.  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.  The kidneys are
atrophic bilaterally.  The stomach and visualized loops of small and large
bowel are grossly unremarkable.  Small amount of intraperitoneal fluid is
again seen and appears unchanged.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  The bladder is partially decompressed and
therefore incompletely evaluated but grossly unremarkable.  The seminal
vesicles and prostate are grossly unremarkable.  There is no free fluid.  Few
colonic diverticula do not demonstrate inflammation.  The appendix is normal.

Visualized bony structures are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No CT evidence for acute intra-abdominal process.  Stable trace
ascites.  Liver heterogeneity which may be secondary to congestion,
particularly in the setting of right atrial enlargement.  Bilateral pleural
effusions, right greater than left persist.

INDICATIONS:  ___ male with end-stage renal failure and axillary
brachial graft with gram-positive bacteremia.  Please rule out graft abscess
or perigraft fluid collection.

FINDINGS:  The antecubital to axillary graft is patent with arterial
anastomotic velocities of 267 cm/sec.  The venous outflow velocities are 184
cm/sec.

The upper arm portion of the graft appears well incorporated without any
evidence of perigraft fluid.  Over a 5-6 cm length near the arterial
anastomosis just above the antecubital fossa, there is some perigraft edema
present with thickening.  There is no discrete abscess.  This may be
consistent with early graft infection.

IMPRESSION:  Patent left brachial axillary AV graft.  The antecubital portion
of the graft has perigraft edema without discrete fluid collection.  This may
represent early or focal graft infection.

INDICATION:  ___ man with end-stage renal disease, for placement of
temporary hemodialysis catheter.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.  Dr. ___,
the attending radiologist was present and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  1% lidocaine was used for local anesthesia.  50 mcg of fentanyl
was given IV.  Patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored
throughout the procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives
of the procedure written informed consent was obtained.  Patient was brought
to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The right
side of the neck was prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion.
Preprocedure timeout and huddle were performed per ___ protocol.

Ultrasound scan of the right side of the neck revealed an occluded right
internal jugular vein.  The right external jugular vein was widely patent and
seen communicating with subclavian vein.  Under ultrasound guidance external
jugular vein was accessed with hard copy images on file using a micropuncture
needle through which a 0.018 guidewire was advanced into the ___.  Needle was
exchanged for a micropuncture sheath and the wire upsized to ___ wire.
After making appropriate measurements the ___ wire was advanced into the IVC
for stability. Micropuncture sheath was removed and the soft tissue tract
dilated using 8, 10, 12 and 14 ___ dilators.  14 ___ x 20 cm temporary
hemodialysis catheter was advanced over the ___ wire.  Tip of the catheter
was positioned in the right atrium.  The guidewire was removed.  Both ports
aspirated and flushed easily.  A final fluoroscopic chest film was obtained
and stored digitally.  Catheter was secured to the skin using 0 silk sutures
and sterile dressings were applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated placement of 14.5 ___ x 20 cm temporary
hemodialysis catheter via right external jugular vein.  Tip of the catheter
terminates in the right atrium and is ready to use.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  End-stage renal disease.  Low ejection fraction after
arteriovenous fistula removal, currently with shortness of breath and
pulmonary edema.

Portable AP chest radiograph was reviewed in comparison to ___.

The right central venous line has been inserted for dialysis purposes, with
its tip being at the cavoatrial junction.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is
unchanged.  There is minimal interval progression of vascular engorgement but
no overt pulmonary edema is seen.  Bilateral loculated effusions and areas of
atelectasis are unchanged.  No pneumothorax is seen.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease, on
hemodialysis, needs tunneled hemodialysis placement.  Patient has an
indwelling right external jugular venous temporary line which needs to be
tunneled.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.  The attending, Dr.
___, was present and supervising during the entire procedure.

1% buffered lidocaine was used for local anesthesia.  Also, lidocaine mixed
with epinephrine was used in the subcutaneous tissue during tunneling. 
Patient was moderately sedated with 75 mcg of fentanyl and 1.5 mg of Versed in
divided doses throughout the total intraservice time of 35 minutes, during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored by a
trained radiological nurse.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Outlining the risks and benefits of the procedure, a
written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  A pre-procedure
timeout and huddle was performed per ___ protocol.  The indwelling
right-sided catheter was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion
including the right upper anterior chest wall.

The scout image of the chest demonstrated the indwelling temporary
hemodialysis catheter with tip ending in the right atrium.  The securing
sutures at the skin were cut.  Both the ports were aspirated and flushed. 
Amplatz wire was then passed through one of the ports and attempts were made
to cannulate the IVC which were unsuccessful.  The Amplatz wire was then left
in situ within the catheter with tip in the right atrium.

Attention was then directed at creating a subcutaneous tunnel.  Appropriate
catheter length measurements were made using the indwelling catheter.  After
infiltrating the subcutaneous and the skin with lidocaine, a 1 cm transverse
skin ___ was made at the right upper anterior chest wall, through which the
permanent hemodialysis catheter measuring 15 ___ x 23 cm cuff-to-tip was
then tunneled towards the venotomy site from where it was brought out.  The
cuff was retracted well within the subcutaneous tunnel.  The Amplatz wire was
then exchanged for the braided J wire was provided in the hemodialysis
catheter kit which was used to cannulate the IVC.  Over this wire, the
indwelling catheter was gently pulled out.  Over this wire, a 15 ___
peel-away sheath was then placed with tip in the right atrium.  Through this
peel-away sheath, the hemodialysis catheter was threaded in, and the peel-away
sheath was peeled out.  The venotomy site was then closed with ___ Vicryl
subcuticular sutures.  The catheter was secured at the skin with 0 silk
sutures and sterile dressings applied.  Both the ports were flushed and
aspirated easily and sterile caps were placed.  Final fluoroscopic scout image
demonstrated the tip to be within the right atrium.  There are no kinks or
malalignment in the tube.  The patient withstood the procedure well and had no
immediate complications and was shifted to the floor in stable conditions with
POE orders.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated conversion of a temporary right external jugular
hemodialysis line to a tunneled hemodialysis line(23 cm cuff to tip).  The
line is ready for use.
